title: incident: add handoff timer, silence windows and SLO-aware auto-mute
author: Maya Chen
description:
Context and motivation: On-call handoffs at Redwood often require manual status announcements and temporary muting of noisy alerts. This PR introduces a lightweight handoff timer (reminders at preconfigured intervals) and a "silence windows" feature that allows the on-call engineer to quickly suppress non-actionable alerts for a bounded period. The silence windows are SLO-aware: the bot consults SLO slackness from slo-toolkit and prevents auto-mute if doing so would risk violating tight SLO guardrails. Goal: reduce cognitive load during handoffs, make temporary alert muting explicit and auditable, and reduce pager fatigue while preserving SLO safety.

What this PR does (summary): - Adds a /hand-off command that starts a configurable timer and posts scheduled reminders (e.g., "handoff begins in 5m, 1m, now") to the incident channel. - Adds a /silence-window <duration> [reason] command to create a short-lived suppression for non-critical alerts; records metadata to audit log and emits an event to the observability channel. - Integrates with slo-toolkit to query current breach risk: if an SLO is within a configurable threshold (<5% error budget remaining), the bot will either block the silence or require an explicit override with a justification. - Persists silences in Redis with TTL and stores an audit entry in the incident-bot audit index. - Adds unit and integration tests around timing edge cases and SLO query failures (fallback: conservative deny).

Checklist: - [x] Design doc referenced (Linear ENG-7812) - [x] New commands implemented and documented in /help - [x] Basic RBAC: only users in oncall-role or SRE team can start handoff or silence - [x] Audit log entries for all creates/extends/cancels - [x] Tests added (unit + integration) - [x] E2E manual verification in staging done 2026-02-22

Small snippets included inside changed files to illustrate intent: - silence window audit entry shape (stored as redis JSON string): {"id":"...","created_by":"...","duration":"10m","reason":"handoff","slo_check":"ok"} - handoff reminder template: "Handoff timer: %s remaining. Please finalize commit messages, update runbook link."

Review conversation (high level): - Arjun Patel (reviewer): "I like the SLO-aware default. Two concerns: 1) what happens if slo-toolkit is unavailable? 2) can we tighten RBAC so only 'primary-oncall' can muting by default?" - Author reply (Maya): "Fallback path implemented: if slo-toolkit fails or times out we conservatively deny silence unless override flag is present and requires a justification that is stored in audit. RBAC updated to check primary-oncall or SRE role; added tests." - Fiona Gallagher: "nit: message text is a bit verbose in the channel; prefer single-line summary with a link to details." - Author reply: "Reworked templates to single-line with expand/collapse link to details (see web/docs/commands.md)." - Diego Ramos: "approve after test coverage for TTL expiry and race with extend/cancel." - Author: "Added integration tests for concurrent extend/cancel; CI passing locally."

Merge strategy and outcome: - Requested rebase to keep history clean; final merge performed with squash merge by Arjun Patel on 2026-02-24. Merge commit: 0c9a8e2 - Release notes: "Added incident handoff timer and SLO-aware silence windows. Admins can configure thresholds and enable/disable the feature via incident-bot settings. See ENG-7812 for behavioral details."

Backward compatibility and safety: - Default behavior is off for orgs who haven't opted in; feature flag added: INCIDENT_HANDOFF_ENABLED=false by default. - Existing alerting and muting APIs remain unchanged. - Breaking change: none.

Operational notes and follow-ups: - Follow-up ticket ENG-7900: add telemetry counters for mute attempts vs allowed vs denied (to track misuse) - Follow-up ticket ENG-7901: dashboard for active silence windows and audit search - Ops runbook: short section added to runbooks/oncall.md describing how to override a blocked mute and where audit entries are stored.

If you want to test: 1) enable feature flag in staging 2) run /hand-off 10m 3) run /silence-window 15m "handoff" and observe audit index and SLO check logs.
